Transport Modes

Transpaleta

A manual or powered wheeled device used to lift and move pallets over short distances in warehouses, terminals, or transport vehicles; recognized under EN 1757-2 and OSHA standards.

Quick answer: A manual or powered wheeled device used to lift and move pallets over short distances in warehouses, terminals, or transport vehicles; recognized under EN 1757-2 and OSHA standards.

Questions and answers

Questions and answers

What is Transpaleta?

In this glossary, Transpaleta refers to: A manual or powered wheeled device used to lift and move pallets over short distances in warehouses, terminals, or transport vehicles; recognized under EN 1757-2 and OSHA standards.

How is Transpaleta used in logistics?

In logistics communication, this term appears in contexts such as: "Los operadores no deben exceder la capacidad nominal de la transpaleta al transportar mercancías, según los manuales de seguridad del almacén."

Why does Transpaleta matter in logistics?

Transpaleta matters because it supports clear communication in Transport Modes contexts for Freight Forwarders, Supply Chain Managers, and Customs Brokers. It also connects to aviation training and exam language such as FIATA Diploma, CILT Certification, and IATA DGR.

Who uses Transpaleta?

Transpaleta is mainly used by Freight Forwarders, Supply Chain Managers, and Customs Brokers.

What category does Transpaleta belong to?

In this glossary, Transpaleta is grouped under Transport Modes. Related pages in this category explain adjacent procedures, commands and operational concepts.

Where does this definition come from?

This definition is sourced from Incoterms 2020 (ICC), FIATA, IATA DGR, WCO and published by Protermify Logistics as a static logistics reference page.

Definition

A manual or powered wheeled device used to lift and move pallets over short distances in warehouses, terminals, or transport vehicles; recognized under EN 1757-2 and OSHA standards.

Operational example

Operators must not exceed the rated load capacity of the pallet jack when transporting goods, as stated in warehouse safety manuals.
